correctness.rationale: Read the actual Downey–Jockusch–McNicholl–Schupp primary Theorem 2.1 (Δ²-set densities are exactly Δ³ reals), Lemma 3.4 (density scaling), and Theorem 5.1 (computable nondecreasing unbounded mind-change bound retains the Δ² density spectrum). For r∈[0,1], a rational baseline a can be chosen in [max(0,r−d),min(r,1−d)], giving u=(r−a)/d∈[0,1] still Δ³. Theorem 5.1 constructs a g-c.e. density-u set on S; a periodic computable baseline of density a/(1−d) on its complement uses ≤1 change; disjoint union realizes r and reverse inclusion is immediate. Both endpoints r=0,1 are valid. Fifteen independent rational boundary decompositions checked; logical content is primary-theorem application, not finite testing.

originality.rationale: Downey–Jockusch–McNicholl–Schupp (2013) proves full Δ² density spectrum for globally computable nondecreasing unbounded f (Thm 5.1) and an exact density-scaling lemma (3.4). The assessed positive-density computable reservoir criterion is a direct but nontrivial new sufficient composition: high changes only on S, one change off S, a rational baseline to reach arbitrary density. It is not the source theorem in altered notation: the full f may oscillate indefinitely and is nowhere globally eventually nondecreasing (explicit alternating example). The source did not state that criterion; a simple pre-existing corollary in broader literature remains possible.
residual_risks: A previously published simple corollary or folklore coding on computable positive-density subsets might subsume the sufficient criterion.
Only rational density d and computable S are covered; arbitrary nonmonotone f not classified.
